98606a3b1f15:
~ The Holy Confessors of Transylvania, Martyrs of the true faith ~

> Two priests, two monks and two free peasants...
Six holy Transylvanian confessors, martyrs of the true faith of their forefathers, in an icon painted on glass: saints in whom the whole Orthodox Church of Transylvania is embodied – hierarchs and clergy, monks and hermits, the faithful...

> The Orthodox Church of Transylvania was (over the centuries) a martyr Church. Countless were the wrongs done by the masters of Transylvania (from the 18th century on) to the Transylvanian Church (including its servants and its faithful), but many too were the valiant fighters who defended the Orthodox faith of their forefathers against the oppression of the imperial power in Vienna. These fighters were: Oprea Miclăuș (a peasant from Săliște, near Sibiu), who suffered death for the true faith; the hieromonks Visarion Sarai and Sofronie of Cioara (near Orăștie); the priests Moise Măcinic of Sibiel and Ioan of Galeș (all five celebrated on 21 October); Atanasie Todoran of Bichigiu, in Bistrița-Năsăud (celebrated on 12 November); and many, many other men, women and children.
> The icon was painted to order, so it is not available. It can be made again, to order.

210acc1f8bff:
~ The Annunciation – icon painted on glass (model: Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century) ~
Because I look forward with emotion to the day of "the Annunciation", because on this DAY (3 years ago) I began to paint icons on glass, because I am grateful... I am showing you an icon (on this theme) painted recently.

The theme of this icon (model: Șcheii Brașovului, mid-19th century) is the Annunciation (celebrated by the Orthodox Church every year on 25 March), the day on which the Holy Archangel Gabriel brings to Earth the news of the Birth of the Son of God. He comes to a town in Galilee (called Nazareth), to a virgin betrothed to a man (named Joseph), announcing to her that she will give birth to the Messiah. The virgin's name was Mary – the Holy Virgin Mary. The good news given to mankind about the incarnation of the Son of God in fact completes our personal feast, our own annunciation.
429b6ce8e571:
✤ 25 March – The Annunciation ✤

Father Cleopa: «Who can understand what depth of humility there was in the heart of the All-holy Virgin Mary, who, hearing and understanding from the Archangel Gabriel that she would conceive of the Holy Spirit and give birth to the Son of God, did not exalt herself in her heart, but with great humility, considering herself a simple handmaid, said: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord. 9ea0843203b5:
~ Jesus with the Vine – icon painted on glass (model: Nicula, 18th century) ~

An icon on glass carries a double charge: the spiritual and the purely aesthetic. The icon "Jesus with the Vine" in this depiction (model: Nicula, 18th century) carries a deep spiritual charge through its very theme... “I am the true vine..." And an aesthetic charge through its vivid colours, its oversized decorations and (sometimes) its painted frame – a charge that "comes" from the old icons (whose models we paint after), icons that we must respect not only as objects of worship but also as historical testimonies.
34c8ab812040:
The Table of Paradise, or the Heavenly Feast – icon painted on glass (model: Nicula, early 19th century)

The icon is not available; I will paint it for a new order. I will paint it either like this icon or (for a personalised icon) with the two saints in the lower rhombuses replaced by any other two saints.

About the icon

The iconographic theme divides the space of the composition into five rhombus-shaped fields, separated by bands decorated with the « rope motif ». The rope (or spiral) motif symbolises infinity.
The central rhombus and the triangular fields next to the five rhombuses hold oversized floral motifs.
Leaning on the sides of the middle rhombus are the four rhombuses showing the guests taking part in the heavenly feast. The Mother of God with the Child and Jesus Christ blessing with His right hand are always in the upper rhombuses; the others hold other saints, in this case Saint Paraskeva (the most venerated of the women martyrs) and Saint Nicholas the Hierarch.

~Icon on glass ”The Ascension of the Lord”~ (model: workshop in Nicula, first half of the 19th century)
~Would you like a similar icon? Contact me and we will settle the details. The icon whose photo I am showing you today has already (for a few hours now) been in a holy and beautiful Church.~

The Orthodox Church celebrates the Ascension of the Lord 40 days after the Resurrection, on the Thursday of the sixth week after Easter. This feast is also known as Ispas. The Ascension of the Lord is the day on which Christians greet one another with “Christ has ascended!” and “Truly He has ascended!“. On this day our Saviour Jesus Christ rose into heaven from the Mount of Olives.
